{
  "buy_saas": {
    "research": "Wrote `/home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/buy_microsaas_research.md`.\n\nMarketplace survey (live, fetched 2026-07-01/02): Acquire.com ($500M+ closed, 2,000+ sold, $2B+ buyer funds, 81-day avg close, smaller SaaS sells faster) and Empire Flippers ($589.6M/2,640 sold) are real and at scale. Live listings captured: EF #94153 (B2B SaaS, $377K ask, $11.8K/mo, 32x monthly — but distressed, −37%/−50% YoY); Microns.io in-budget SaaS (~$120K for ~$40K/yr rev, ~3x rev), with the cheapest \"SaaS\" being AI-wrapper junk priced on hope (11.6x rev on $864/yr). Real multiples: Acquire median 3.9x annual profit; FE International 5-7x SDE under $2M. The pricing truth confirms 3-3.5x = buying decline; a fair 4-4.5x on his $80-150K budget buys only ~$1.5-2.5K/mo net.\n\nDiligence: source-verify via read-only Stripe+bank three-way reconcile, self-built cohort curve, IP/code-doc checks (FE calls poor code docs \"deal-killing\"), <20% concentration; eight specific deal-killer red flags listed. Churn reality: FE sample avg 4.7%/mo (~44%/yr) — base case is flat-to-decline.\n\nDeal structure: all-cash + 10-30% earnout/note + escrow + non-compete + 60-90d transition; AVOID SBA/personal-guarantee (it destroys the capped downside that is the idea's whole point).\n\nDelegation trap quantified: the affordable asset ($1.5-2.5K/mo) can't afford a $1-2.5K/mo VA+dev; the worth-delegating asset ($4K+/mo) costs >$150K. True net after his time ≈ $0-2.5K/mo. Resolution: engineer net up himself (hosting cuts, dunning, one AI feature) rather than delegate a small asset. Verdict stands CONDITIONAL; do the ~$0 dry-run first.",
    "plan": "Wrote `/home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/buy_microsaas_PLAYBOOK.md` — a week-by-week 90-day plan built on the research and prior validation.\n\nStructure:\n- **Gate 0 (Day 0)**: the pass/fail personal-fit test — 20-25 hrs/wk in months 1-6, 8-12 indefinitely; defer if CutLog is mid-crunch. Plus locking 1-2 verticals and accepting the 4-4.5x multiple reality.\n- **The Buy Box**: hard-filter target profile (vertical B2B system-of-record, ~4.5%/mo churn baseline, <20% concentration, AI-safe), with concrete niches and his edge reframed as diligence alpha, not value-creation alpha.\n- **Days 1-20**: marketplace accounts (Acquire/EF/Flippa/Microns), exact saved-search filters ($75-160K, SaaS, B2B, $2-5K/mo net, 18+ mo), reusable diligence toolkit, 20-30 listings/wk routine → shortlist 5-8.\n- **Days 20-50**: screen → source-verify (read-only Stripe+bank three-way reconcile, self-built cohort curve) → code/infra audit → the eight deal-killer red flags → narrow to 1-2, underwrite at 4-4.5x.\n- **Days 50-75**: LOI + structure (all-cash bulk + 10-30% earnout/note + escrow + non-compete + 60-90d transition; avoid SBA/PG), escrow diligence, close.\n- **Days 75-90**: do-no-harm absorption, self-serve net-lift moves (hosting cut, dunning), and the delegation setup.\n\nKey honest numbers baked in: budget ~$95-140K all-in; ~13-22% gross cash yield netting ~$0-2.5K/mo true profit after his time; a 12-month P&L showing **no VA+dev line** because the delegation-affordability check (affordable asset $1.5-2.5K/mo can't fund $1-2.5K/mo delegation; worth-delegating $4K+/mo asset costs >$150K) proves it would go negative. Verdict remains CONDITIONAL with a ~$0 dry-run first."
  },

    {
      "name": "Compressed Air Leak Detection",
      "slug": "compressed_air_leaks",
      "revised_score": 3.6,
      "verdict": "PASS",

      "competitors": [

      ],
      "kill_risks": [
        "OEM bundling: Atlas Copco SMARTAIRNET / Kaeser KMT deliver wireless demand-side leak analytics from the vendor already in the compressor room at near-zero CAC — uncontestable distribution",
        "Free substitute: utility rebate audits + free compressor-dealer leak surveys already give the buyer the headline ROI for $0",
        "Hardware/cert/inventory wall outside founder's domain (PCB/RF/FCC-CE/enclosure/RMA) at 10-20 hrs/wk solo — most likely pre-revenue stall point",
        "Front-loaded value vs recurring price: leaks found once, high SaaS churn after first fix cycle; $200/mo stream unproven",
        "Commodity analytics: ML '$/month per leak' is already a stock feature of a $3-5K CS Instruments LD500 handheld — no moat"
      ]

    {
      "name": "Fire Sprinkler Inspection App",
      "slug": "fire_sprinkler",
      "revised_score": 3.6,
      "verdict": "PASS",
      "economics": "Cash to a credible MVP is $200-225K (doc's own BOM: 6-mo runway + mandatory iOS-dev hire + domain-expert contract) — at/over the founder's $25-150K ceiling and requiring two hires for skills he lacks; NOT a nights/weekends build.         "SafetyCulture (iAuditor) — $2B+ general inspection platform, configurable for fire",
        "NFPA (standards body) — running its own AI projects for sprinkler placement / ceiling-height estimation"
      ],
      "kill_risks": [
        "'Empty quadrant / zero competition' is FALSE — Inspect Point (15K users, 4.5M inspections), ServiceTrade (1,300+ customers), and BuildingReports (13M+ inspections) already own the platform, the NFPA-25 workflow, the photo/deficiency capture, the proprietary labeled corpus, AND branded AI. A CV head-recognizer is a copyable feature, not a product.",
        "Seat price is fiction: market is $0 office-users / ~$75 per tech (ServiceTrade) or $299/mo flat for a whole team (FireLab); WTP for a bolt-on recognizer is a small fraction of the assumed $199-399/seat. Revenue math off ~1000x.",
        "Founder-fit inverted + two mandatory hires — non-domain, no iOS, no trade network; the hard non-delegable work (domain credibility, trade trust, distribution) is exactly his weakness. $200K+ and >15 hrs/wk, not a solo build.",
        "Cold-start data wall — needs proprietary labeled deficiency photos he can only get from the conservative customers he can't reach; the doc's own Gate-1 kill risk is likely to trigger.",
        "Conservative, liability-sensitive, slow-adopting buyer — 3-6mo trust-based sales cycles; NFPA mandate makes buyers warier of unproven outsider AI, not more eager."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tracka_plan_validation": [
    {
      "slug": "compressed_air_leaks",
      "plan_holds": "HOLDS-WITH-CHANGES",
      "weakest_assumptions": [
        "Gate 3 recurring-revenue thesis: buyers will pay $200/mo ONGOING after leaks are fixed. Almost certainly wrong — value is front-loaded (leaks found once); the entire incumbent market sells periodic surveys, not subscriptions. If wrong, the SaaS thesis collapses to one-time services-with-a-detector.",
        "Gate 0 addressable slice: that ≥100 plants exist that are non-OEM-managed AND in a no-free-audit utility zone AND have serious air spend AND will buy from an unknown solo vendor. The carve-out is defined by the absence of the very signals of a serious air spender, so the slice is thin/self-defeating; likely fails at Week 2 for $0.",
        "Success probability ~10-15%: chaining four gates each rated 'likely fails/coin-flip' plus a solo hardware build plus a cold-sales ramp yields ~3-7%, not 10-15%. EV is even closer to zero.",
        "'$5K kit + $200/mo' economics: the kit is mostly COGS + install labor (near break-even, not profit), CAC for cold industrial sales by an unknown solo founder is $2-5K/plant, and front-loaded value implies 30-50%+ annual churn — so recurring net is ~$400-700/mo at best, not scalable margin.",
        "Part-time-safe: true only in the validation phase. Phase B (field installs/calibration/RMA + daytime cold industrial sales, and firmware/RF if built) is 15-25 non-delegable, largely-daytime hrs/wk — incompatible with a full-time job and the 10-20 hr/wk constraint."
      ],
      "revised_monthly_profit": "$0/mo base case (80-90% probable). Optimistic ~3-7% tail: $400-700/mo net recurring at 18-30 months after $45-110K capital, declining with churn, never nearing the $5-30K/mo target. Probability-weighted expectation ~$30-60/mo (effectively zero).",
      "revised_verdict": "PASS",
      "confidence": "HIGH"
    },
    {
      "slug": "fire_sprinkler",
      "plan_holds": "HOLDS",
      "weakest_assumptions": [
        "PWA avoids the iOS hire and 'iPads run web fine' — most likely wrong: field offline/burst-photo capture in dead-zone stairwells and basements is exactly what iOS Safari PWAs are worst at (no background sync, storage eviction, camera quirks); losing this collapses the plan's ≤$75K build-cost claim back toward $60–90K with a re-incurred iOS-native hire.",
        "'Equity/rev-share domain partner solves distribution + data + credibility' (T1/G1) — an active NICET-IV inspector or shop owner good enough to bring a book of business and proprietary photos is scarce and won't easily join an unproven non-domain remote AI side-project for equity; risk is a WEAK partner passing G1 as a false positive. Fix: require an ACTIVE client base, not just 'credible'.",
        "'General multimodal models can't do the core task zero-shot' (the hoped-for T4) — GPT-5/Gemini-class vision increasingly does head-type ID and paint/corrosion flagging zero-shot, so G4 most likely FAILS and the CV moat evaporates (forcing a pivot to a smaller NFPA-25 structured-logic layer).",
        "'≥5 shops put money down at ≥$40/seat within 10 weeks' (G3) contradicts the plan's own 3–6 month trust-based sales cycle for a still-on-paper conservative trade; realistically resolves at week 14–20 or never, most likely as soft verbals with zero signatures.",
        "'Plan B (license CV module to an incumbent) is lowest-time, highest-EV' — Inspect Point holds 4.5M labeled inspections + 15K-user distribution and already ships two AI products, so its rational move is build-not-buy; Plan B is a low-probability lottery, not high-EV."
      ],
      "revised_monthly_profit": "~$0/mo base case (modal outcome is a ≤$5K validation kill; even if it survives to month 24 the mandatory ~$1–1.5K/mo domain retainer swamps a ~$1,250/mo top line to break-even/slightly negative). Low-probability (<10%) upside ~$2–3K/mo at ~80 seats. Does not reach the $5–30K/mo goal on any realistic path.",
      "revised_verdict": "PASS",
      "confidence": "HIGH"
    }
  ]
}

Read /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/FLAT_SHOWDOWN.md for the existing honest ranking (buy-SaaS 5.2, CutLog 4.5, hosting 4.5, fab-shop 4.4, bookkeeping 4.3, exam 3.5, licensing 3.0; Compressed Air/Fire Sprinkler were the only UNVERIFIED rows — now resolved).

WRITE /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/FLAT_SHOWDOWN_V2.md with: (1) the updated full ranked table with Compressed Air & Fire Sprinkler now at their RED-TEAMED scores (no longer estimates); (2) did either Track-A idea beat the buy-SaaS pick (5.2)? 1	# FLAT SHOWDOWN — All Serious Secondary-Income Candidates, One Honest Scale
2	
3	**Created**: 2026-07-02 by Claude (Opus 4.8). **Owner**: Hooman Shariati (hshariati@adobe.com).
4	
5	**The rule of this document**: zero sunk cost, zero incumbent protection. CutLog is ONE
6	candidate for Hooman's single serious-venture slot — not a protected baseline. "It would
7	distract from CutLog" is NOT a mark against any other idea; CutLog must earn the slot on
8	merit like everything else.
9	
10	**Founder**: Adobe eng manager; AI/ML + cloud + infra; EE; mech-eng friends; $25–150K capital;
11	~10–20 hrs/wk; wants $5–30K/mo secondary income; AI-safe preferred; open to any shape and to
12	abandoning CutLog.
13	
14	**Comparability note**: CutLog and the fab-shop/Plasma platform were just red-teamed
15	(revised scores 4.5 / 4.4). The 5 Track-B ideas were honestly revalidated
16	(`DEEP_DIVE_SYNTHESIS.md`). The two Track-A #2s (Fire Sprinkler 6.70, Compressed Air 7.65)
17	are shown at their **un-red-teamed optimistic** scores and are explicitly **discounted** here
18	by the same pattern that cut CutLog (false "no/low competition" premise, gross-read-as-profit,
19	top-decile-as-base-case) — because every idea that HAS been red-teamed lost 2–4 points to
20	exactly those flaws. Their honest scores below are estimates pending an actual red-team.
21	
22	---
23

# FLAT SHOWDOWN V2 — All Serious Secondary-Income Candidates, One Honest Scale

**Created**: 2026-07-02 by Claude (Opus 4.8). **Owner**: Hooman Shariati (hshariati@adobe.com).
**Supersedes**: `FLAT_SHOWDOWN.md` (v1). The only substantive changes vs v1: the two Track-A
ideas that were still shown at *estimated* discounted scores — **Compressed Air Leak Detection**
and **Fire Sprinkler Inspection** — have now been actually red-teamed, planned, and validated.
They are shown here at their **real red-teamed scores (both 3.6)**, no longer estimates. Buy-SaaS
now also carries a detailed 90-day acquisition playbook.

**The rule of this document**: zero sunk cost, zero incumbent protection. CutLog is ONE
candidate for Hooman's single serious-venture slot — not a protected baseline. "It would distract
from CutLog" is NOT a mark against any other idea.

**Founder**: Adobe eng manager; AI/ML + cloud + infra; EE; mech-eng friends; $25–150K capital;
~10–20 hrs/wk; wants $5–30K/mo secondary income; AI-safe preferred; open to any shape and to
abandoning CutLog.

---

## 1. The single ranked table (all candidates, comparable honest basis)

| # | Candidate | Honest monthly profit (net) | Capital | hrs/wk | Shape | Honest score /10 | Verdict | Key reason |
|--:|-----------|------------------------------|---------|--------|-------|:---:|---------|------------|
| 1 | **Buy a cash-flowing micro-SaaS** | $0–2.5K base; $5–7K only if rare fair-priced sticky asset | $95–140K all-in | 20–25 (mo 1–6) → 8–12 | Buy + operate | **5.2** | CONDITIONAL | Only idea whose primary input is *capital*, not his hours; capped downside; playbook now written |
| 2 | **CutLog (Laser Param SaaS)** | $200–700 base (hobby); $2.5–7K only in ~15% upside | ~$0 build / time is the cost | 8–15 (non-delegable) | Pure SW | **4.5** | CONDITIONAL | Best BUILD fit, but free live clone (lasertips.org) + OEM tables kill the moat & WTP |
| 3 | **Managed hosting (buy, not build)** | $1.5–4K in 18–30mo; ~40–50% chance $0 | <$25K build / $40–100K buy | ≤6 → 5–10 | Buy/build SW-ops | **4.5** | CONDITIONAL | No clean target niche (UniFi double-covered, n8n license-gated); real moat is community/sales |

| 5 | **Vertical bookkeeping SaaS** | $3–6K net *if* it survives to mo 18–24; EV < $2K | <$10K | 8–12 | Services+SW | **4.3** | CONDITIONAL | Edge is relationships/trust (his weakness); niche already saturated (Kruze/Zeni/Pilot) |
| 6 | **Compressed Air Leak Detection** *(now red-teamed)* | **$0/mo base (80–90%); $400–700/mo net only in ~3–7% tail after $45–110K** | $50–150K (HW+SW) | 15–25 in build/field phase | HW+SW | **3.6** | **PASS** | OEM bundling (Atlas Copco/Kaeser) + free utility/dealer audits + HW/FCC wall outside his domain |
| 7 | **Fire Sprinkler Inspection** *(now red-teamed)* | **~$0/mo base (modal ≤$5K validation kill); $2–3K/mo net only in <10% tail** | $200–225K + 2 hires | >15 (non-solo) | Pure SW | **3.6** | **PASS** | "Empty quadrant" is FALSE — Inspect Point (15K users), ServiceTrade, BuildingReports own it; two mandatory hires; founder-fit inverted |
| 8 | **Exam-prep course** | $0–1K yr 1; $0–2K at mo 12 w/ real chance negative | $5–9K one-time + $3–6K/mo burn | 10–15 (mo 1–6) | Content/SW | **3.5** | PASS | 12–24mo SEO/YouTube grind vs entrenched specialists; proof is a 2016 outlier |
| 9 | **Royalty licensing (inventRight)** | $0/mo yr 1 near-certain; $0–few-hundred EV | ~$600 DIY → ~$6K | 4–8 active weeks | Invention licensing | **3.0** | PASS | Right-skewed lottery; as *reliable income* it is $0; both cited proofs collapse |

**What changed from v1**: In v1, Compressed Air sat at an *estimated* ~5.0 (optimistic 7.65) and
Fire Sprinkler at an *estimated* ~4.5 (optimistic 6.70), both flagged UNVERIFIED. The red-team
confirmed the predicted haircut almost exactly: both land at **3.6 / PASS**. Compressed Air fell
harder than its estimate (the hardware/cert wall + OEM bundling are worse than the discount
assumed); Fire Sprinkler fell to roughly its estimate. **Neither is now a top-4 idea.**

---

## 2. Did either Track-A idea beat the buy-SaaS pick (5.2)?

**No. Decisively no.** Both came in at **3.6**, a full **1.6 points below** buy-SaaS and below
CutLog, hosting, the fab-shop platform, and bookkeeping. Each collapsed on the *same* pattern
that has cut every red-teamed idea in this project:

- **False "empty quadrant / low competition" premise.** Fire Sprinkler's headline "zero
  competition" is simply false — Inspect Point (15K users, 4.5M inspections, $28M raised),
  ServiceTrade (1,300+ customers), and BuildingReports (13M+ inspections) already own the
  NFPA-25 workflow, the photo/deficiency capture, the labeled corpus, *and* branded AI. Compressed
  Air faces Atlas Copco SMARTAIRNET, Kaeser KMT, UE Systems, Fluke, CS Instruments, Prosaris —
  plus free utility-rebate audits and free dealer surveys.
- **Gross read as profit.** Both pitches quoted top-line ($200/mo × N + kit; $199–399/seat) as if
  it were net. Kit is mostly COGS/support; realistic seat price is $50–80 (or $0 office / ~$75/tech).
- **Top-decile treated as base case.** Fire Sprinkler pitched $1.79M ARR yr1 (off by ~1000x);
  Compressed Air pitched a $1.6K capital build (real is $45–150K).
- **Founder-fit / capital reality.** Fire Sprinkler needs $200K+ and *two* hires (iOS + domain
  expert) for skills he lacks — not a solo build; the non-delegable hard part (trade trust,
  distribution) is exactly his weakness. Compressed Air needs a solo hardware/RF/FCC build outside
  his domain plus daytime industrial cold-sales — incompatible with a 10–20 hr/wk evening constraint.

Buy-SaaS remains #1 because its lever is **capital, not his scarce evening hours**, and its
downside is **capped** by an all-cash + earnout/escrow structure (no SBA/personal guarantee).

---

## 3. Profiles + headline plans for the three ideas Hooman asked about

### 3A. Buy a cash-flowing micro-SaaS — #1, score 5.2, CONDITIONAL
*Research: `runs/buy_microsaas_research.md`. Playbook: `runs/buy_microsaas_PLAYBOOK.md`.*

**Profile.** Deploy $95–140K all-in to acquire an existing vertical B2B SaaS rather than build.
Marketplaces are real and at scale (Acquire.com: $500M+ closed, 2,000+ sold, 81-day avg close;
Empire Flippers: $589.6M / 2,640 sold). **Honest economics**: a fair 4–4.5x multiple on his budget
buys only ~$1.5–2.5K/mo net, ~13–22% gross cash yield. Churn reality is harsh (FE sample avg
4.7%/mo ≈ 44%/yr), so the base case is **flat-to-decline**. The **delegation trap** is the core
catch: the affordable asset ($1.5–2.5K/mo) can't fund a $1–2.5K/mo VA+dev, while the
worth-delegating asset ($4K+/mo) costs >$150K — so true net after his time ≈ **$0–2.5K/mo**.
Resolution: engineer net up *himself* (hosting cuts, dunning, one AI feature), not delegate.

**Headline plan (90-day, from the playbook).**
- **Gate 0 (Day 0)** — personal-fit pass/fail: can he give 20–25 hrs/wk in months 1–6 (8–12 after)?
  Defer if CutLog is mid-crunch. Lock 1–2 verticals; accept the 4–4.5x reality.
- **Days 1–20** — open Acquire/EF/Flippa/Microns accounts; saved searches ($75–160K, SaaS, B2B,
  $2–5K/mo net, 18+ mo history); build reusable diligence toolkit; 20–30 listings/wk → shortlist 5–8.
- **Days 20–50** — source-verify (read-only Stripe + bank three-way reconcile, self-built cohort
  curve), code/infra audit, the eight deal-killer red flags; narrow to 1–2; underwrite at 4–4.5x.
- **Days 50–75** — LOI + structure (all-cash bulk + 10–30% earnout/note + escrow + non-compete +
  60–90d transition; **avoid SBA/personal guarantee**); escrow diligence; close.
- **Days 75–90** — do-no-harm absorption; self-serve net-lift moves; delegation setup.
- **First**: run the ~$0 dry-run (2–3 real listing diligence passes) before committing capital.

### 3B. Compressed Air Leak Detection — #6, score 3.6, PASS
*Red-team + plan validation now complete.*

**Profile.** HW+SW: acoustic/ultrasonic sensor kit + ML "$/month per leak" analytics for plants.
**Economics**: base case **$0/mo** (stalls at the hardware/FCC-cert/field-reliability wall or loses
every deal to a free audit / OEM-bundled analytics). Only a ~3–7% tail reaches $400–700/mo net
recurring at 18–30 months after **$45–110K real capital** (not the pitched $1.6K), and it declines
with churn. Probability-weighted expectation ≈ **$30–60/mo (effectively zero)**.
**Kill risks**: (1) OEM bundling — Atlas Copco SMARTAIRNET / Kaeser KMT ship wireless demand-side
leak analytics from the vendor already in the compressor room at near-zero CAC; (2) free utility
rebate audits + free dealer leak surveys already hand the buyer the headline ROI for $0; (3)
solo hardware/RF/FCC/RMA build outside his domain; (4) value is front-loaded (leaks found once) so
the $200/mo recurring stream is unproven; (5) the analytics are already a stock feature of a
$3–5K CS Instruments LD500 handheld — no moat. **Plan verdict: HOLDS-WITH-CHANGES → PASS (HIGH
confidence).** Weakest assumption: that anyone pays $200/mo *ongoing* after leaks are fixed.

### 3C. Fire Sprinkler Inspection App — #7, score 3.6, PASS
*Red-team + plan validation now complete.*

**Profile.** Pure-SW mobile app: CV head-recognition + NFPA-25 deficiency capture for inspectors.
**Economics**: cash to a credible MVP is **$200–225K** (its own BOM: 6-mo runway + mandatory
iOS-dev hire + domain-expert contract) — at/over his ceiling and needing **two hires** for skills
he lacks; not a nights/weekends build. Year-1 net ~$0 (likely negative). Base case at 24 months
**~$0/mo** (modal outcome is a ≤$5K validation kill); even if it survives, a ~$1–1.5K/mo domain
retainer swamps a ~$1,250/mo top line to break-even. <10% tail: ~$2–3K/mo at ~80 seats.
**Kill risks**: (1) "empty quadrant" is FALSE — Inspect Point / ServiceTrade / BuildingReports own
the platform, workflow, corpus, and AI; a CV recognizer is a copyable *feature*, not a product;
(2) seat price is fiction — market is $0 office-users / ~$75 per tech / $299/mo flat, so revenue
math is off ~1000x; (3) founder-fit inverted — non-domain, no iOS, no trade network; (4) cold-start
labeled-photo data wall he can only cross via the conservative customers he can't reach; (5)
liability-sensitive, slow-adopting buyer wary of unproven outsider AI. **Plan verdict: HOLDS → PASS
(HIGH confidence).** Weakest assumptions: PWA-avoids-iOS-hire (offline burst-photo capture is
exactly Safari PWA's weakness) and that a strong domain partner will join an unproven side-project
for equity.

---

## 4. Final recommendation — the one venture slot

**Nothing changed the v1 call. If anything, it is now firmer.** The two Track-A ideas were the last
unverified rows and the only remaining candidates that could have out-ranked buy-SaaS. Both were
red-teamed to **3.6 / PASS** — well below the buy-SaaS **5.2**. There is now **no build idea in the
field that out-ranks buying a cash-flowing micro-SaaS**, and specifically **the honest "build" pick
named in v1 (Fire Sprinkler) is now dead** — it needs $200K+ and two hires and faces three
entrenched platforms.

**Recommendation (unchanged, now with the details Hooman asked for):**
1. **Do not treat CutLog as the serious-venture slot.** Demote it to a ≤2 hrs/wk hobby/optionality
   project; keep the ~15% industrial upside alive without letting it claim the slot.
2. **The merit pick for the $25–150K is the buy-a-micro-SaaS path** — the only candidate whose lever
   is capital, not his scarce evening hours, with capped downside and a written 90-day playbook.
3. **Freeing CutLog's focus is what makes buy-SaaS viable** — the two decisions are linked, because
   Gate 0 requires 20–25 hrs/wk for 6 months.
4. **Run the ~$0 dry-run first.** Confirm on 2–3 real listings that a fair-priced $2–4K/mo asset can
   be run at <10 hrs/wk without a VA+dev spend that eats the profit. If the dry-run shows the
   delegation trap is unbeatable, buy-SaaS collapses toward the hosting idea's ~40–50% chance of $0
   and *no* idea in this field earns a full GO — in which case the honest answer is "don't deploy
   the slot yet."

**Bottom line**: On an honest, sunk-cost-free scale, **buy a cash-flowing micro-SaaS (5.2)** remains
the best use of the one venture slot; **free CutLog's focus to enable it**; **do the dry-run before
committing capital**. Compressed Air and Fire Sprinkler are confirmed PASSES — not the secondary
stream Hooman wants.
